subject: Direct reading ecology
source: Lovejoy Recent Literature in Philosophy and Ethics AJT 8.2 pp395-405
documented_finding: Lovejoy reviews twelve recent works spanning French religious philosophy psycho-sociological ethics pragmatism and history of philosophy.
evidence_limit: Reading/reviewing does not by itself establish personal contact or intellectual dependence.

subject: Pragmatism and intellectual responsibility
documented_finding: Lovejoy warns that popular pragmatism can become a plenary absolution from intellectual responsibility and says its limits and practical application must be carefully defined.
evidence_limit: Does not amount to a general rejection of pragmatism.

subject: Natural ground versus demonstration
documented_finding: Lovejoy says the teleological argument may remain a natural ground of theistic belief while never amounting to strict demonstration.
evidence_limit: Theological evaluation should not be conflated with historical proof standards without explicit comparison.

subject: Laberthonniere French religious philosophy
documented_finding: Lovejoy directly reviews Laberthonniere's Paris 1903 Essais and reconstructs its non-compulsive theory of truth while criticizing the attempted reconciliation with external church authority.
evidence_limit: Proves active reading of a current French work not personal contact or Paris transmission.

subject: Duprat translation control
documented_finding: Lovejoy refuses confidently to judge Duprat's meaning and merits from a hopelessly bad English translation and reconstructs likely French syntax to recover the proposition.
evidence_limit: Hypothetical source-language reconstruction remains Lovejoy's critical repair not access to the original demonstrated in the review.

subject: Linguistic fact versus moral conclusion
documented_finding: Lovejoy argues that even a clear common usage of good would not without further argument establish the grounds or content of moral obligation.
evidence_limit: Does not imply ordinary language is irrelevant to moral analysis.

subject: Antecedents and influence as distinct historical tasks
documented_finding: Lovejoy criticizes Hume and Rousseau studies for insufficient treatment of antecedents and downstream influence while separately praising textual exposition.
evidence_limit: Does not establish any single preferred causal model.

subject: Analytical history criterion
documented_finding: Lovejoy praises Norman Smith for tracing determining Cartesian assumptions through logical working-out vicissitudes weakening and replacement and calls the result analytical history.
evidence_limit: Praise of method does not establish direct methodological borrowing.

subject: Couchoud historical milieu and Spinoza classification
documented_finding: Lovejoy calls customary classification of Spinoza as Cartesian misleading identifies more distinctive affinities elsewhere and praises Couchoud for reconstructing a many-sided historical milieu rather than treating Spinoza in vacuo.
evidence_limit: Affinity must not be collapsed into direct historical borrowing.

subject: Couchoud French methodological comparator
source: Couchoud Benoit de Spinoza Paris Felix Alcan 1902 preface
documented_finding: Couchoud says he follows rules applicable to history of philosophy; his first rule is to consider everything Spinoza wrote rather than preselect only properly philosophical works.
evidence_limit: External comparator only; no proof Lovejoy adopted this rule from Couchoud.

subject: Laberthonniere publication control
source: Open Library and library catalog records
documented_finding: Essais de philosophie religieuse was published in Paris by P. Lethielleux in 1903.

subject: Duprat French-English publication control
documented_finding: Duprat's La morale appeared in Paris in 1901 and an English translation Morals appeared in 1903.
evidence_limit: Does not prove which edition Lovejoy consulted beyond his explicit review of the English translation.
